prompt:
Use case: product-mockup.
Asset type: final ultra-wide luxury fragrance collection website hero photograph, approximately 2.4:1 landscape aspect ratio.
Input images 1, 2 and 3: authoritative product identity references for AMBER HOUR, OPEN SKY and IRON CROWN respectively; each is a contact sheet, use its large FRONT-VIEW bottle only. Do not reproduce contact sheets.
Create one restrained, art-directed, physically believable high-perfumery campaign photograph of all THREE After Bells bottles. Inspired by the architectural composition and disciplined product lighting of the great perfume houses such as Amouage, Creed and Clive Christian, with an original After Bells set.
Scene: a real studio set with two low, substantial dark honed-limestone blocks, one slightly higher, against a deep charcoal-brown seamless backdrop. A quiet warm light grazes the stone; the rest of the background is a nuanced near-black espresso. No castle, arches, smoke, floating particles, dramatic gold glow or theatrical props. Subtle realistic stone grain, soft contact shadows, a small natural reflection on the darker surface.
Composition: the LEFT 44 percent of the photograph is clean dark negative space for a website heading, with no bottle or props there. Group all three bottles elegantly in the RIGHT 50 percent, arranged as an asymmetrical but balanced trio at slightly different depths/heights, all front-facing and each label unobstructed. AMBER HOUR on the left of the group, OPEN SKY at the centre slightly forward, IRON CROWN on the right. All three bottles are the same physical model and size. Their caps start around 22 percent from the top edge, glass bases end around 77 percent from the top. Keep every cap and glass base fully visible with generous border safety. The group must look composed by a still-life photographer, not a flat catalogue lineup.
Product invariants: retain the exact supplied thick clear rectangular faceted flacons, bevelled shoulders, short gold collar, heavy transparent glass base and ornate SQUARE GOLD CAP engraved with the same symmetrical floral filigree. Amber Hour has rich amber liquid; Open Sky has pale green-gold liquid; Iron Crown has muted warm brown-amber liquid. Retain the earlier SMALL, delicate irregular gold flakes mostly resting near the bases, with only a few suspended. Do not enlarge them.
Front labels: thin square satin gold plaques attached flush to glass, fine physical edges and realistic reflected studio light; exact double fine dark border. The black uppercase wordmark "AFTER BELLS" is serif. Below is a small line-diamond-line divider, then the clean uppercase sans-serif fragrance name, respectively "AMBER HOUR", "OPEN SKY", "IRON CROWN". Maintain the label geometry and typography of the references, no new symbols or invented text. NO stickers or plaques on narrow sides. Labels and bottle sizes consistent across all three.
Photography: broad diffused key light from upper left, soft frontal bounce keeping the ink readable, negative fill defining glass edges, a modest backlight through the liquids. Natural softbox reflections and subdued satin metal highlights. Optical glass must read as glass, not chrome or plastic. Controlled highlights, realistic shadow falloff and restrained colour grading. Medium-format still-life photograph, 120 mm lens, f/11, ISO 100 character; sharp labels, tactile detail, gentle backdrop falloff. Avoid HDR, oversharpening, glowing edges, computer-render shine, illustrated textures or synthetic gold gradients.
No text anywhere outside the three existing front labels, no watermark, no extra bottles, no packaging. One unified photograph.
scope: Collection hero only; individual product photographs retained.
